newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open weak, struggling at 2,100.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open weak, struggling at 2,100.

text.p: Singapore shares opened weak on Friday and the key Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) was struggling to hold its support at the 2,100 level, dealers sadi.
"There is not much action. Foreign funds are still selling Singapore blue chips although in small amounts," said a dealer.

At 0130 GMT, the STII was down 8.79 points to 2,101.78, after dipping just below 2,100 to 2,099.71 in the early minutes. Market activity was slim with just 12.1 million shares with losers ahead of gainers by 38 to 25.
Most of the volume was due to block trades including in newly listed NatSteel Broadway.

NatSteel Broadway saw one million shares crossed at US$0.69 and was trading at US$0.655, below its initial offer price of US$0.70. Singapore Telecom saw 1.2 million shares crossed at Singapore S$3.089 (US$2.20).

Trading firm Causeway saw 2.8 million shares crossed, the bulk at S$1.50. It announced on Thursday that three of its major shareholders sold a total of 9.82 million shares. It topped the actives with 2.5 million shares including the block trades and was flat at S$1.42. Cerebos Pacific led the index down with a loss of S$0.20 to S$10.70. Jurong Shipyard and UOB foreign fell.
